subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the straight line through (3, −4) whose x-intercept and y-intercept are in the ratio 2 : 3.

mark_split.label: Write the intercept form with one unknown

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 8, book p.141. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for turning the ratio into a single unknown k and writing the intercept form, and the second for substituting the point and clearing k. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked by substitution: 3(3) + 2(−4) − 1 = 9 − 8 − 1 = 0, so (3, −4) lies on 3x + 2y − 1 = 0; its intercepts are 1/3 and 1/2, and (1/3) : (1/2) = 2 : 3, so both conditions in the question hold.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how the ratio becomes one unknown, and where the given point is used.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the intercept form with one unknown
steps.margin_note: First mark. A ratio 2 : 3 does not fix the two intercepts, only their proportion, so write them as 2k and 3k and carry one unknown instead of two.
steps.memory_tip: A ratio gives one unknown, not two: intercepts in the ratio 2 : 3 are 2k and 3k.
lines: The intercepts are in the ratio 2 : 3

recall.must_convey: That the intercepts are taken as 2k and 3k and put into the intercept form x/a + y/b = 1.
accept: take the intercepts as two k and three k
use the intercept form x by a plus y by b equals one
the ratio gives one unknown k
intercepts ni two k three k ga teesukovali
write x by two k plus y by three k equals one
reject: substitute the point three minus four
heard_as: x by a plus y by b

steps.why: The intercept form is the only standard form that shows both intercepts directly, so a condition on the intercepts can be written into it at once.
common_mistakes: Taking the intercepts as 2 and 3 instead of 2k and 3k.
Writing the intercept form as ax + by = 1.

steps.label: Use the point and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The point gives one equation in k. Multiplying through by 6k clears both denominators in one move.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply by the LCM of the denominators, here 6k, so no fractions are left to slip on.

recall.must_convey: That substituting (3, −4) gives k = 1/6, the intercepts 1/3 and 1/2, and the line 3x + 2y − 1 = 0.
accept: put three and minus four into the equation
multiply by six k to get nine minus eight
point substitute chesthe k one by six vasthundi
the line is three x plus two y minus one equals zero
reject: take the intercepts as two k and three k

steps.why: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal, so x/(1/3) becomes 3x and y/(1/2) becomes 2y, which clears the last fractions.
common_mistakes: Writing x/(1/3) as x/3 instead of 3x.
